author: Tsuchiya
name_in_asr: 陀歴 (Faxian); プグッチ遺跡 Pouguch/Poguch site (Stein's Lohilo Kot; locally 'University')
asr_identification: Pouguch (Poguch) site on a terrace c. 125-130 m above Pouguch village, left bank of the Darel river, 15.3 km above its confluence with the Indus, Darel valley (Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan): the temple of Faxian's wooden Maitreya
evidence: Surface survey of 1998 (no excavation): an irregular enclosure of red-earth walls (W 98 m, S 25 m, E 79 m, N 43 m), the red earth said by villagers to come from near Atth 30 km upstream; a 3 m road along the E wall; two square stone gate-post bases 17 m apart (main gate) with a small stone-lined basin by a rock opposite; inside, a single mound of cut stones under earth at the highest point facing the gate, taken for the main temple, with a sloping open area of c. 70 m to its N. No barracks or thick stone buildings, so not the fort Stein (1913) took it for. The site lies in the safest part of the valley, near the mouth, far from the passes at the head (Yajei, Batakhun) by which enemies entered. No image, inscription or datable find; she cannot say how the 24 m image related to the mound (perhaps an open-air statue).
quote: プグッチ遺跡(地図 M-2)は,西流するインダス川の峡谷で合流するダレル川の河口から15.3km 遡った標高1360mのプグッチ村の高台 (最高地点 標高1490m)にある。…1913年,オーレル・スタインは,この遺跡 (P-2) をロヒロ・コット Lohilo Kot と呼…正門の正面にあたり,敷地内で最も高い地点に,切り石が山積みになったまま土砂に被われたような, 小高い土塁があった。
note: Agrees with the study and Mizutani on the valley (Darel, medium) and narrows it to a site. Faxian's 陀歴 is her subject throughout; Xuanzang is not mentioned, though his 達麗羅川 has the same wooden Maitreya. The evidence is a walled enclosure with one mound, seen on the surface: no matching monument has been found, so it does not meet the study's rule for high. Answers in part Neelis 2011 ('no remains found'): a candidate site, untested by excavation.

author: Tsuchiya
name_in_asr: 陀歴; プグッチ遺跡
asr_identification: Pouguch site, Darel valley, as above
evidence: Interviews (planned 2008, held January 2009, by Taj Rehmat in Shina, under Amjad Ayub) with seven men of Pouguch aged 26-78, each at home, not told the purpose or of Faxian; repeating an informal group session of 1998. All call the site a Buddhist temple; all but one speak of a great Buddha image, mostly of gold (8 to 28 tons); one says wooden, one (a religious scholar who claims descent from its builder, king Udar of the Soodow clan) gives its height as 24 m; pilgrims came from China, Russia, Tibet, Central Asia. None knew of Faxian or Chinese pilgrims. The villagers call the site 'University'.
quote: 本聞き取り調査によって,『法顕伝』 にある陀歴についての記述の主要な点のすべてが,プグッチ遺跡について村民の間に伝えられた内容と一致していることが判明した。…法顕の訪れた陀歴が,広義でダレル渓谷, 狭義ではプグッチ遺跡であろうと推定することへの第一歩が踏み出せた。
note: Oral tradition, not site evidence. She argues that the valley's isolation kept it uncontaminated, but the name 'University', the 24 m figure (= Faxian's 八丈) and the wood are the kind of detail that could come from outside; she herself calls the result a 'first step'. Adds nothing to the confidence of 03.01.16 (medium).

author: Tsuchiya
asr_identification: Faxian's route from Tashkurghan to Darel: Khora Bort pass - Karambar - Ishkoman - Gakuch - Singal valley, bypassing Gilgit
evidence: Her surveys of 1991-2007 of the passes and valleys between the Little Pamir and Darel; Buddhist finds at Gakuch and Bubur; Faxian, she argues, went straight to Darel because he does not mention Gilgit.
note: Faxian's route, not the location of a Xiyu ji place; Xuanzang reached Darel from Udyana and only heard of Bolor (03.02). Context for Kuwayama's 5th-century pilgrims' road through Ishkoman (03.02 note), not evidence for Bolor's site.
